title: Australian Government Endorsed Events (Workplace Justice Pilot) (Temporary Activity visa (subclass 408))

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: This temporary visa allows you to extend your stay in Australia to pursue a workplace exploitation claim.

sections.heading: Overview > You must
sections.text:
- apply online
- be in Australia, but not in immigration clearance
- hold a temporary substantive visa with work rights, with no more than 28 days remaining; or have held a temporary substantive visa with work rights that has ceased within 28 days
- have certification of your workplace exploitation claim from a participating government agency or an accredited third party, see Eligibility
- maintain adequate health insurance during your stay in Australia

Help with your visa

If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on Who can help with your visa application

sections.heading: Overview > With this visa, you can
sections.text:
- remain temporarily in Australia to pursue your workplace exploitation claim
- include members of the family unit in your visa application, if they are in Australia.

sections.heading: Overview > How long you can stay
sections.text: 6 months (or up to 12 months, depending on your circumstances)

sections.heading: Overview > Processing time
sections.text:
For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool. This will show the processing times for recently decided applications. It is a guide only and not specific to your application.

Find out what you can do to help us process your application faster.

sections.heading: About this visa > With this visa, you can
sections.text:
- Stay in Australia temporarily, to pursue your workplace exploitation claim
- Include members of the family unit in your visa application, if they are in Australia.

The Workplace Justice Pilot will have two phases implemented over two years, and has been designed to enable temporary migrants to remain in Australia while they seek workplace justice.

sections.heading: About this visa > How long you can stay
sections.text:
This is a temporary visa.

Your circumstances will determine how long you can stay. We will tell you the length of your visa in your visa grant letter.

Your visa stay period starts the day we grant it and is shown on the visa grant letter. The visa stay period does not restart each time you re-enter.

You can check your visa details in the visa grant letter or use VEVO.

sections.heading: About this visa > Stay longer
sections.text:
You can’t stay longer in Australia by extending this visa.

If your workplace exploitation claim has not been finalised before your visa expires, you may be eligible to apply for another visa.

You cannot reuse your original workplace exploitation claim certification when applying for another visa. You must give us new certification from a participating government agency or an accredited third party.

If your workplace exploitation claim is finalised and your visa is about to expire, you should plan to leave Australia.

If you wish to stay in Australia, you will need to apply for and be granted another type of visa. See Explore your visa options.

sections.heading: About this visa > Include family
sections.text:
You can include members of the family unit in your application when you apply.

Family members who apply for the visa with you must also meet our health and character requirements.

Newborn Children

If you had a baby that was born in Australia, you must tell us about your child as soon as possible (even if they don't have a passport yet). You can’t include your baby in your application for this visa until you tell us. See How to tell us if you had a baby.

sections.heading: About this visa > Cost
sections.text:
There is no visa application charge for this visa.

You might have to pay other costs, including health checks and police certificates.

Family members added to your application after you apply must pay a subsequent temporary application charge.

To work out what your visa will cost, use the visa pricing estimator. The estimator does not take into account the other costs.

sections.heading: About this visa > Processing times
sections.text:
For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool.

Your application can take longer to process if:

- you do not fill it in correctly
- you do not include all the documents we need or we need more information from you
- it takes us time to verify your information.

Processing times are available through Global Visa Processing Times.

sections.heading: About this visa > Use of information
sections.text:
We may disclose the information you provide to us to other Commonwealth, State and/or Territory bodies as outlined in the Home Affairs’ Privacy Notice (Form 1442i).

The information we disclose may include your personal information (including biometric information and other sensitive information) and details of the workplace exploitation you have experienced.

This is to enable Home Affairs, including the Australian Border Force and other relevant agencies, to undertake investigation and/or enforcement related activities. The aim is to enhance employer compliance to reduce workplace exploitation.

The information that is disclosed may include information about the place of employment where the workplace exploitation is alleged to have occurred. If you are an employer, find out more about migrant worker protections.

sections.heading: About this visa > Your obligations
sections.text:
You and your family must follow all visa conditions and Australian laws.

Learn more about conditions for this visa.

sections.heading: About this visa > Visa label
sections.text:
We will digitally link your visa to your passport. You will not get a label in your passport.

If we grant you a visa, we will send you a grant notification letter containing the visa grant number. You can use this number to access your digital visa record.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be in Australia
sections.text: You, and any family members who apply with you, must be in Australia to lodge an application for this visa.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have a substantive visa that has no more than 28 days remaining or that expired less than 28 days ago
sections.text:
To be eligible for this visa you must:

- hold a temporary substantive visa with work rights with no more than 28 days remaining or
- have held a temporary substantive visa with work rights that ceased within 28 days of lodging your application.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have certification of your claimed workplace exploitation matter and you are committed to seeking justice or redress within a timely manner
sections.text:
You must give us certification from a participating government agency or an accredited third party. This must explain why it is beneficial or necessary for you to stay in Australia to pursue your workplace exploitation claim.

Types of workplace exploitation may include:

- underpayment of wages
- pressure to work more hours than your visa conditions allow
- pressure to give your passport to your employer
- your employer threatening to cancel your visa
- bullying or harassment (including sexual harassment).

Only a participating government agency or an accredited third party can certify your claim. See Who can certify your claim.

If you need to stay in Australia for up to 12 months, a lawyer who holds specialist accreditation from the relevant Law Society of their State/Territory in employment law, or has 5+ years of experience practicing for an accredited third party, must provide your certification.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be able to support yourself and any dependants
sections.text: You must be able to support yourself and any dependant family members with you in Australia.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet the health requirement
sections.text:
You, and any family members who applied for the visa with you, must meet our health requirement.

We will let you know if you or your family members must undergo a health check.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet our character requirement
sections.text:
You, and any family members aged 16 and over who applied for the visa with you, must meet our character requirement.

We will let you know if you or your family members must undergo character checks.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have adequate health insurance
sections.text:
You are personally liable for all your healthcare costs while you are in Australia. Medical insurance helps limit your financial liability.

You must have adequate health cover for the whole of your stay to be granted this visa. Your cover should cover you for medically necessary treatment, including transport.

See what we consider adequate health insurance.

See more about health insurance for overseas visitors.

Reciprocal healthcare agreements

Some countries have a reciprocal healthcare agreement with Australia. Find out more from the Department of Human Services about reciprocal healthcare agreements.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be a genuine temporary entrant
sections.text:
You can't use our temporary visa program to maintain ongoing residence in Australia.

The genuine temporary entrant (GTE) requirement helps us to make sure that you use temporary visas correctly.

We must be satisfied that you have a genuine intention to stay here temporarily.

When assessing your application, we will consider:

- your situation
- your immigration history
- compliance with visa conditions
- any other relevant matter.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have consent to be granted the visa
sections.text: We will only grant this visa to a child younger than 18 years if all persons who have parental responsibility for them have given their consent for us to grant the visa.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Best interests of the child
sections.text: We might not grant this visa if it is not in the best interests of an applicant under 18.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have paid back debt to the Australian Government
sections.text: If you owe the Australian Government money, you must have paid it back or have a formal arrangement to pay it back.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Not had a visa cancelled or an application refused
sections.text:
We will consider your immigration history when we make a decision on your application. If you have had a visa cancelled or refused you might not be eligible for this visa.

In some circumstances you may still apply for a permanent visa if you have had a visa cancelled or an application refused. See Limitations on applications in Australia.

If applying for a visa from outside Australia, see Can I go to Australia.

If you want immigration assistance, see Who can help with your visa application.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Sign the Australian values statement
sections.text: If you are 18 years of age or older, you must acknowledge the Australian values statement that confirms you will respect the Australian way of life and obey Australian laws when you apply for the visa. Learn more about Australian values.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply
sections.text:
Report your workplace exploitation to a participating government agency or an accredited third party so they can help you resolve your workplace exploitation claim, including certifying your claim.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Get help with your application
sections.text:
Only some people can help you with your application. If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance they must be:

- a registered migration agent
- a legal practitioner, or
- an exempt person.

You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf relating to your visa application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents
sections.text:
Give us evidence to support your application, including certification of your workplace exploitation claim.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Certification of your workplace exploitation claim
sections.text:
You must have certification given by a participating government agency or an accredited third party. See Who can certify your claim.

You must attach the certification when you lodge your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Provide accurate information
sections.text: Provide accurate information. See what happens if you can't prove your identity or don't provide true information.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Identity documents
sections.text:
Give us the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details, and passport issue and expiry dates.

Also give us:

- a national identity card, if you have one
- proof of change of name.

Documents that prove a change of name include:

- a marriage or divorce certificate
- change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority
- documents that show other names you have been known by.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Financial documents
sections.text:
You must show us you can support yourself by providing:

- evidence of your current or upcoming employment, such as an employment contract or job offer; or
- other evidence of your financial position.

We can also consider bank statements, allowances, and accommodation.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Character documents
sections.text: We will tell you if and when you need to get a police certificate.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Tell us you are getting help
sections.text:
To nominate someone to:

- receive your correspondence, use Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient

- provide immigration assistance, use Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Additional documents for applicants under 18
sections.text:
Applicants under 18 years old must give us:

- copies of birth certificates or the family book showing the names of both parents
- copies of the adoption paper, if applicable.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Applicants under 18 parental responsibility documents
sections.text:
You must get consent for any applicant under 18 years of age to visit Australia from anyone who:

- has a legal right to decide where the applicant lives and
- is not coming to Australia with the applicant.

They must complete either:

- Form 1229 Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years (276KB PDF), or
- a statutory declaration giving their consent for the applicant to visit Australia on this visa.

Alternatively, you can show us:

- an Australian court order that allows the applicant to visit Australia, or
- that the laws of your home country allow them to visit

Include:

- an identity document that shows the signature and photo of the person who completed the form or declaration, such as a passport or driver’s licence
- adoption papers or other court documents if applicable.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Translate
sections.text:
Have all non-English documents translated into English.

Give us original and translated documents in your application.

Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters.

Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. However, on each translation, they must include their:

- full name
- address and telephone number
- qualifications and experience in the language they are translating.

These details must be in English.

Note: You do not need to have any documents certified.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Scan or photograph
sections.text:
Scan or photograph all documents (English and non-English) in colour.

The scans and photos must be clear.

If a document is more than one page, save it all as one file.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Attach
sections.text:
Attach a document only once, even if you are using it to show more than one thing.

Learn more about attaching documents.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa
sections.text:
You must apply for this visa online. You must be in Australia, but not in immigration clearance, when you apply.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > Provide accurate information
sections.text: You must give us accurate information. See what happens if you can't prove your identity or don't provide true information.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > Apply online
sections.text:
- Create an account or login to ImmiAccount.
- Attach documents
- Pay the application fee (if required).
- Note the transaction reference number (TRN).

Each family member must have their application fee paid, if required, and documents attached to their application.

Any family members who apply with you must be in Australia, but not in immigration clearance, when you apply.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply
sections.text:
We will let you know when we have received your application. See what you can and must do after you apply.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Status updates
sections.text:
We can’t give updates on applications within the standard processing time.

You can check if we need more information from you in ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Stay lawful
sections.text:
If you are in Australia, make sure you stay lawful by holding a visa while we process your application.

If you were in Australia when you applied for this visa you may be granted:

- a Bridging visa A (BVA) if you held a substantive visa when you applied
- a Bridging visa C (BVC) if you did not hold a substantive visa when you applied.

If your current visa expires before we decide on your application, the Bridging visa will start. You can stay in Australia on the Bridging visa while we process your visa application.

You can check your conditions and the expiry of your current visa in VEVO.

You can’t re-enter Australia on a BVA or BVC, they will cease when you leave Australia. If you plan to travel outside Australia while we are processing your application, you might need to apply for and be granted a Bridging visa B (BVB), see Bridging visa B (BVB) before you leave Australia.

Do not ask to have the visa you currently hold cancelled. If your visa is cancelled:

- You will be staying in Australia unlawfully
- Your bridging visa will cease.

Learn more about visa expiry.

Check what conditions might apply to your bridging visa or the visa you have applied for with our condition checker.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Travel
sections.text:
If you leave Australia after you have submitted your application but before we have made a decision, make sure you have a visa to return.

If you plan to travel outside Australia while we are processing your application, you might need to apply for and be granted a Bridging visa B (BVB), see Bridging visa B (BVB) before you leave Australia.

Check your conditions and the expiry of your current visa in VEVO.

Learn about visa expiry.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Health exams
sections.text:
If you didn't have health examinations before you applied, we will let you know if you need them.

Check ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Health insurance
sections.text: It is a condition of your visa that you maintain adequate health insurance during your stay in Australia. See Health Insurance.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Biometrics
sections.text: We might ask for biometrics (fingerprints and photo). We will let you know if you must provide them.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Attach more information
sections.text:
If you did not attach all documents when you applied, attach them as soon as possible in ImmiAccount.

We might also ask you to give us more information.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Add family
sections.text:
You cannot add members of the family unit to your application after you have applied. If you do not include them in your application, your family members must apply separately.

To apply separately, your family members need to complete an application for a Temporary Activity, International Relations or Training Visa (Subsequent entrant) (403,407,408) form in ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Subsequent entrants
sections.text:
If we grant you the visa, your family members can apply to stay in Australia with you as subsequent entrant.

To apply as a subsequent entrant, your family members must be in Australia and need to complete an application for a Temporary Activity, International Relations or Training Visa (Subsequent entrant) (403,407,408) form in ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Newborn children
sections.text: Find out what to do if your child is born after you apply.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Mistakes on your application
sections.text:
Let us know as soon as you can if you made a mistake on your application.

Complete Form 1023 Notification of incorrect answers and attach it in ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Help with your application
sections.text:
Let us know if you no longer want someone to:

- receive your correspondence - complete Form 956a Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration advice - complete Form 956 Advice by a migration agent/exempt person of providing immigration assistance

- act for you - let us know in writing by uploading your advice in ImmiAccount.

See more about withdrawing your nomination.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
Things you must let us know about after you have applied might include:

- changes to your phone number, email, address or passport
- changes to your marital or de facto status
- the birth of a child

- you want to withdraw your application.

For more information on what to do if things change, see How to tell us if your situation changes.

If your circumstances have changed since you applied, and you no longer need this visa, you must withdraw your application.

If you do not withdraw your application, this visa may be granted and as a result, any other substantive visa that you may hold will cease at the time we grant this visa.

See How to withdraw an application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Visa outcome
sections.text:
We will let you know our decision in writing.

If we grant your visa, we will tell you:

- Your visa grant number
- Your visa stay period
- The date your visa starts
- Your visa conditions, if applicable.

If we refuse your visa, we will tell you:

- Why we refused the visa
- Whether you have a right to a review of the decision.

Keep a copy of the decision.

We will not refund the application fee if we refuse your application. See Refunds.

New step description

sections.heading: When you have this visa > In Australia
sections.text:
What you can do when you have this visa

- Stay in Australia temporarily to pursue your workplace exploitation claim

- Travel outside Australia and return as many times as you want during your visa stay period.

To see your specific conditions and work entitlements use VEVO.

What you must do on your visa

You must not stop pursuing your workplace exploitation claim.

If you stop pursuing your workplace exploitation claim, you may have to leave Australia or apply for and be granted a new visa to remain in Australia.

You must meet all visa conditions and follow Australian laws.

Check your conditions on your visa grant letter or in VEVO.

Visa condition 8107 – Information for visa holders

For Workplace Justice visa holders there are no work restrictions, as long as it does not prevent you from pursuing your workplace exploitation claim.

You can:

- work in any occupation or industry, anywhere in Australia
- change employers, or work for more than one employer (including self-employment)

Note: You do not need to tell us about any changes in your employment.

Workplace rights and entitlements

Temporary visa holders with permission to work are protected by Australian workplace law. See your workplace rights and entitlements.

To see your conditions for work, use VEVO.

Tell us if things change

Things you must let us know about include:

- changes to your phone number, email, address or passport
- changes to your relationship status
- the birth of a child.

See how to tell us if there is a change in your situation

See how long you can stay

The visa stay period starts on the date the visa is granted.

You can check your visa stay period in your visa grant letter or use VEVO.

The stay period does not restart each time you re-enter Australia.

To see when you must leave, use VEVO.

Staying longer

You can’t stay longer in Australia by extending this visa.

If your workplace exploitation claim has not been finalised before your visa expires, you may be eligible to apply for another visa.

You cannot reuse your original certification. You must give a new certification from a participating government agency or an accredited third party. This must explain why you need to stay longer in Australia.

If your workplace exploitation claim is finalised and your visa is about to expire, you must apply for and be granted another type of visa to stay in Australia. For more information see Explore your visa options.

Travelling on your visa

You can travel outside Australia and return as many times as you want during the visa stay period.

Time spent outside Australia does not extend the visa.

The visa stay period does not restart each time you enter Australia. Any time you spend outside of Australia counts as part of the stay period.

See your visa stay period or conditions in VEVO.

Proving you have a visa

To prove you have a visa and show your conditions to someone, use VEVO.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Leaving Australia
sections.text:
Before you leave

Check your travel documents

You must have a valid passport or other travel document to leave Australia.

Ensure your visa is still in effect

Check your conditions and the expiry of your current visa in VEVO.

See what you can and must do if your visa has expired or is about to expire.

At the border

Departures SmartGate

We have an automated process that uses facial recognition technology and your ePassport. You might be able to leave the airport faster if you use SmartGate.

After you leave

Proving you have been to Australia

To get proof of your travel in and out of Australia request your international movement records .
